subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and should it be modeled as selfDeny, delegateOnly, scoped allow entries, or folded into per-spawn toolsAllow work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change adds public config surface and changes how tool-deny security boundaries flow from requester agents to subagents.

options.title: Approve Delegate-Only Config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Fold Into Per-Spawn Policy
options.body: Let sessions_spawn.toolsAllow own child restriction and document that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate profiles or prompt guidance.

options.title: Keep Monotonic Policy Only
options.body: Reject parent-deny delegation and document the security rationale plus separate-agent workarounds.

recommendation.title: Approve Delegate-Only Config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public security-boundary config decision, and Peter is the strongest available routing signal from CODEOWNERS and issue timeline activity.
